findings.detail: Arax current-period source maturity is 3/24/2032, but the identifier carries the prior-period 4/11/2029 maturity while retaining the current-period S + 5.25% spread.
Redwood source maturity is 6/16/2032, so the conflicting structured value 1/10/2033 is assigned from a different instrument or context.

rationale: The raw current-period schedule resolves representative flagged rows. Arax proves a comparative-period field merge: its current row states S + 5.25% and 3/24/2032, whereas the flagged identifier combines that current spread with 4/11/2029, a date appearing only on the comparative schedule. Redwood proves that the opposite stored side can also be wrong: its source row states 6/16/2032, not the structured 1/10/2033 value. Thus the rule is detecting real row/context assignment defects rather than issuing a false alarm.
